headline: CRUDE SPLITS FROM DIESEL AS HARVEST STALLS IN THE RAIN
lead: WTI settled $91.26 Friday, down 1.5%, while Dated Brent physical barrels reportedly cleared $120 the same day as Hormuz tanker strikes (ongoing since the Iran war began) widen the crude-diesel split. That spread is why your diesel bill isn't following the crude headline down.
teaser: Diesel is pricing like a shortage while crude isn't, and harvest rain just made that gap matter.

one_number.unit: LNG cargoes exiting Hormuz in September
one_number.context: Highest monthly count since the Iran war began but still below pre-war levels, a sign the physical fuel system is strained, not fixed.

yesterdays_call.note: Crude closed $91.26, down again and under the $87.50 line's spirit of the call; the Gulf-flow break kept extending into Friday.
yesterdays_call.call_line: Called crude down toward $87.5 ($89.37 when the call was made). It closed at $91.26.

action: Diesel buyers: lock the next 30 days of on-farm fuel now; WTI at $91.26 says cheap, physical diesel markets say otherwise.

sections.title: Crude Down, Diesel Up, Same Barrel
sections.body: - WTI settled **$91.26** Friday, off 1.5%, even as oilprice.com reports Dated Brent physical crude cleared $120 on droned Hormuz tankers and a G7 plan to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude reserves over four months.
sections.so_what: Diesel, not crude, is the input cost farmers actually feel this fall.

sections.title: Harvest Stalls, Basis Stays Put
sections.body:
- Corn eased to **$4.97**, down 0.4%, and beans ticked up a penny to $12.77 as AgWeb reports record El Nino rain is stalling harvest across the country.
- Basis sits at seasonal lows per the seasonal calendar, and wet fields mean no fresh farmer selling to test it either direction.
sections.so_what: No harvest pressure yet means basis has nothing forcing it off the floor.

outside_the_pit.title: Farm Bureau Asks Trump For Diesel Tax Relief
outside_the_pit.body: Farmers want the federal highway diesel tax suspended and dyed-diesel penalties waived while the fuel squeeze runs through harvest season.

watch_list.desc: Crop Progress; harvest pace below last year's would confirm the El Nino delay is real, not noise.
Watch Dated Brent versus WTI; a widening gap past $29 says the diesel squeeze is deepening, not easing.
Farm bill SNAP standoff in Senate Ag; no deal risk keeps safety-net payments in limbo past harvest.

daily_quote.text: Good judgment comes from experience, and experience comes from bad judgment.

source_summary: CME/CBOT settlement data, USDA, oilprice.com, AgWeb, Feedstuffs, Beef Magazine, Agri-Pulse, The Fence Post
